name: Diagnostic_ALG-BEX_1
generalfeedback: For \(n\) a positive integer then by the binomial theorem \[ \left(a + b\right)^n = a^n + \frac{n!}{\left(n-1\right)!\cdot 1!}a^{n-1}\cdot b + \ldots+\frac{n!}{\left(n-r\right)!\cdot r!}a^{n-r}\cdot b^r + \ldots + b^n\mbox{.} \] In this case \(a={{CT:1}}\), \(b={{CT:2}}\) and \(n=5\); therefore \[\begin{array}{rcl}\displaystyle \left({{CT:0}}\right)^5 = {{CT:1}}^5 + 5\cdot {{CT:1}}^4 \cdot {{CT:2}} \cdot x + \frac{5\cdot 4}{2!} \cdot {{CT:1}}^3 \cdot {{CT:2}}^2 \cdot x^2 + \frac{5 \cdot 4 \cdot 3}{3!} \cdot {{CT:1}}^2 \cdot {{CT:2}}^3 \cdot x^3\mbox{,} \\ + \frac{5 \cdot 4 \cdot 3 \cdot 2}{4!} \cdot {{CT:1}} \cdot {{CT:2}}^4 \cdot x^4 + {{CT:2}}^5 \cdot x^5\mbox{,} \end{array}\] where \[\begin{array}{rcl}\displaystyle 2!&\displaystyle =&\displaystyle 2 \cdot 1 = 2\mbox{,}\\ 3!&\displaystyle =&\displaystyle 3 \cdot 2 \cdot 1 = 3 \cdot 2! = 6\mbox{,}\\ 4!&\displaystyle =&\displaystyle 4 \cdot 3 \cdot 2 \cdot 1 = 4 \cdot 3! = 24\mbox{.} \end{array}\] So \[\left({{CT:0}}\right)^5 = {{CT:3}}\mbox{.}\]
